chunks: And from him (Al-Saduq), from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.ابْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ: Ibn Abi Umayr, a prominent narrator of hadith
key_terms.الْمَسْأَلَتَيْنِ: The two questions, referring to the preceding hadiths

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a Mukatab according to the two preceding questions?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi uses this concise narration to establish legal continuity, linking the status of the *Mukatab* (freed slave) to the preceding rulings on manumission contracts. This cross-referencing technique highlights the systematic nature of early Shia jurisprudence, where specific details are often derived from established principles in adjacent texts. It underscores the importance of contextual reading in hadith compilation, ensuring that the legal framework for social emancipation remains consistent with broader Islamic equity.
